theorems.name: C6 and C12 chiral coordinates
theorems.statement: For G=1+R, H=r(1+G), J=r(R-R^2), R^2+R+1=0 and 3r^2=1, one has 2G=1+3rJ and 2H=3r+J.

theorems.name: Cell-rooted dyadic polygon tower
theorems.statement: Starting from the six-direction rotor K_0=G and repeatedly taking the chirality-selected normalized adjacency root gives K_n of order N_n=6*2^n with K_n^(N_n/2)=-1 and nested vertex sets.

theorems.name: Exact inscribed polygon area
theorems.statement: If K_n=c_n+s_nJ, the regular N_n-gon formed by its powers has area A_n^-=(N_n/2)s_n=3*2^n*s_n.

theorems.name: Exact circumscribed polygon area
theorems.statement: With tau_n=s_n/(1+c_n), consecutive tangents meet at height tau_n and the regular outer polygon has area A_n^+=N_n*tau_n.

theorems.name: Sharp dyadic width contraction
theorems.statement: The exact ratio of consecutive polygon gaps is (1-tau_(n+1)^4)/4, hence it is strictly smaller than 1/4.

theorems.name: Exact C12 baseline
theorems.statement: At the actual twelve-phase Cell/gate layer, c_1=sqrt(3)/2, s_1=1/2, A_1^-=3 and A_1^+=12(2-sqrt(3)).

theorems.name: Unit physical Cell dodecagon
theorems.statement: Since the current physical Cell radius satisfies r^2=1/3, the boundary dodecagon read out from the C12 phase directions has exact area one; the outer tangent dodecagon has area 8-4sqrt(3)=8-12r.

theorems.name: Pi equals three plus algebraic residual completion
theorems.statement: The lower areas increase from A_1^-=3, the upper areas decrease, and their common limit L satisfies L=3+sum_(n>=1)(A_(n+1)^--A_n^-), with 0<L-A_n^-<A_n^-*tau_n^2.

theorems.name: Geometric identification of L
theorems.statement: The nested inner and outer polygons exhaust the unit rotation-character disk, so its area is L; their perimeters converge to 2L, hence circumference/diameter=L. Therefore L is geometric pi.
theorems.boundary: This uses standard real planar analysis but does not use pi as an input to the finite tower.

theorems.name: Cell-rooted finite Euler ladder
theorems.statement: At every level K_n^(3*2^n)=-1. The Cayley form of these exact finite identities converges to exp(JL)=-1, and EMECPP-T10 identifies L with pi.
